name: GSM-R cells
label: GSM-R
notes: GSM-R base stations (GSM for railways, 3GPP GSM), decoded by OnAir's receiver through the onair-rx handler; the row has no decoder of its own, so only a handler runs it. It reads what each cell broadcasts on its BCCH, not calls: a job takes 2 MHz of IQ (the receiver reads 1 MHz at the least) and searches it for 200 kHz carriers (the strongest 12, outside 4 percent of each edge). Each event is a cell, first when it is read and again when a member changes (`snr_db` and a measured `freq_hz` change without a new event): `freq_hz` (the carrier as measured, off the raster), `arfcn` (when the carrier is on the raster of GSM 850, 900, DCS 1800 or PCS 1900), `bsic` (NCC times 8 plus BCC), `mcc`, `mnc`, `lac` and `cell_id` (from System Information 3 or 4; null until read) and `snr_db`. The receiver decodes a stretch of 2.2 s at a time, so an event comes up to one stretch after the signal. Paging and access blocks are counted and not published; traffic is not decoded. Each BCCH block goes to a packet capture as GSMTAP (type 1, Um) in IPv4 and UDP to port 4729 (link type 101). Ranges and bands: GSM-R's downlink 921 to 925 MHz (R-GSM, the railway band at 876 to 880 MHz uplink) is 3GPP TS 45.005's; other railway allocations exist, the receiver reads any GSM 850, 900, 1800 or 1900 MHz carrier, and a job started by hand runs anywhere. The scene the check uses has two cells 1.6 MHz apart, so its centre is 923.0 MHz. Listing bar: measured on the build host (12 cores) through a scratch node's release build, 30 s of the generated capture looping on a file source and fed in real time; the job skipped no input, onair-rx used 0.51 of a core and the node 0.08 of a core (load average 6.1 to 4.8).
